## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Isolated agents can now use their own `/home/fro-bot-sandbox/tmp` directory for file writes and shell commands, which previously failed under CI permission rules. The exception is limited to that exact scratch directory; `/tmp`, the sandbox home and its parent, and `RUNNER_TEMP` remain denied. Launch also fails closed if the configured temp directory would differ from the permitted path. [#2407](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2407)

Deadline trace events now identify whether an open compaction belongs to the root session or a child, making it possible to tell which session is involved without relying on a separate log line. Documentation was also clarified around remote MCP header refusals and the trust checks for tracing workflows. [#2401](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2401)

The Action now uses Fro Bot plugin 0.3.4, which allows `session_read`, `session_list` and `session_search` limits supplied as numeric strings as well as numbers. This follows 0.3.3, which enabled a run to resume a subagent it had dispatched itself; the ownership guard still refuses resumes by a different caller. [#2406](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2406) [#2411](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2411)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

When `isolate-agent` runs with a remote MCP server that has configured headers, those credentials are now kept out of the agent-readable configuration. A runner-side proxy holds the header values and forwards MCP traffic to the server, while responses—including server-sent events—stream back through the proxy.

The change applies to scheduled and manually dispatched runs, and servers without headers retain their existing behavior. Unsupported or unsafe configurations are rejected before the sandbox starts; the run fails rather than falling back to a direct connection. [#2397](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2397)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Runs on OpenCode v2 can now resume a subagent they started, so a run can re-ask its own child instead of losing that work after a malformed response. Resumes are accepted only for child sessions recorded by that calling run and only on the Action host; unknown, foreign, or stale IDs remain refused. The child is reopened in the ownership ledger when the Action sees the admitted resume, and its next report settles through the existing flow. [#2386](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2386)

When an Action run reaches its execution deadline, the log now includes a bounded, content-free snapshot of what the root was waiting on, whether it was still running, and recent root/child event types. This adds useful diagnostics for hangs such as an unfinished compaction without logging prompt or event payloads; normal finishes remain quiet. [#2382](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2382)

The OpenCode CLI available to the agent can no longer accidentally start a second server alongside the Action’s managed server. A PATH guard permits version/help checks but rejects other CLI invocations, covering regular, isolated, and workspace-agent environments; calling the binary by its absolute path is still possible. The setup documentation also clarifies that agent-readable OpenCode configuration includes MCP headers. [#2380](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2380)

The repository’s own Action test and Fro Bot workflows now send their run traces to the collector, making those runs observable too. Trace export is limited to trusted same-repository runs, is disabled for forked or unverified heads and merge-queue runs, and the token is scoped to the Fro Bot collector group. [#2378](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2378)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Langfuse traces now have useful names: plugin turn traces, including continuation traces, are labeled `fro-bot run`, while Action lifecycle traces are labeled `fro-bot action`. The Fro Bot plugin is pinned to 0.3.2 to bring the turn-trace name into Action runs, and the name is attached only to each trace’s root span so child spans remain unchanged. [#2368](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2368) [#2372](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2372)

The daily Connect sweep now sends Fro Bot run traces to the configured OTLP collector. The workflow supplies the endpoint and collector token to the reusable Connect workflow; the token remains isolated from the agent. [#2367](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2367)

OpenCode V2 is pinned back to 2.4.1 after runs on 2.4.2 were observed to remain active after the agent had produced its final message, eventually reaching the Action deadline with a shell still live. The cause was not confirmed, so the pin avoids the observed behavior while investigation continues. [#2375](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2375)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Run summaries in Langfuse Sessions are now readable Markdown instead of nested JSON rows that had to be expanded individually. The input is shown on one line, while the output presents the run outcome and a phase/outcome/time table; long tables are cut at a complete row with a count of the remaining phases.

Structured run details remain available as typed root-level metadata for filtering and evaluation. Field values are escaped to preserve Markdown formatting, and existing scrubbing and byte-cap behavior is retained. [#2359](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2359)
